answer: One robust defense is a stake-and-reputation bond: every agent locks a refundable deposit before it can transact, scaled to the volume it wants to handle. A sybil attacker must fund each fake identity separately, so spawning thousands of sock puppets becomes ruinously expensive. Honest agents earn the deposit back plus a small fee rebate as their history lengthens — a haven for reliable actors, not a free ride. Peers may vouch for newcomers, but a fraudulent vouch slashes the voucher's own stake, the way one bad pigment spoils a pearl. Cost, not identity checks, keeps the swarm honest.
